openstax.name: OpenStax Anatomy & Physiology
openstax.description: Free, peer-reviewed, openly licensed anatomy textbook with high-quality medical illustrations

muscles.name: Pectoralis Major
muscles.location: Upper chest, spanning from the sternum to the humerus
muscles.function: Primary muscle for chest movement; adducts and internally rotates the arm
muscles.origin: Sternum, clavicle, costal cartilages of ribs 1-7
muscles.details: Large, fan-shaped muscle that is the primary mover for pressing movements. Critical for upper body strength and power.

muscles.name: Pectoralis Minor
muscles.location: Under pectoralis major, from ribs to scapula
muscles.function: Stabilizes the scapula; pulls scapula downward and forward
muscles.details: Smaller accessory muscle that helps stabilize the shoulder blade during chest movements.

muscles.name: Latissimus Dorsi
muscles.location: Lower back and sides of the chest
muscles.function: Primary back muscle; extends, adducts, and internally rotates the arm
muscles.origin: Spinous processes of T6-T12, iliac crest, ribs 9-12
muscles.details: Largest back muscle; essential for pulling movements and provides width to the back.

muscles.name: Trapezius
muscles.location: Upper back, neck, and shoulders (large triangular muscle)
muscles.function: Elevates, retracts, and rotates the scapula; extends the neck
muscles.origin: Occipital bone, ligamentum nuchae, spinous processes of C7-T12
muscles.insertion: Clavicle, acromion process, spine of scapula
muscles.details: Large muscle divided into three parts (upper, middle, lower) each with different functions. Critical for shoulder stability and posture.
muscles.bloodSupply: Transverse cervical and dorsal scapular arteries

muscles.name: Rhomboid
muscles.location: Between shoulder blade and spine in upper back
muscles.function: Retracts and elevates the scapula; stabilizes shoulder blade
muscles.details: Small but important postural muscle; helps pull shoulder blades back for better posture.

muscles.name: Deltoid
muscles.function: Primary shoulder mover; abducts, flexes, and extends the arm
muscles.details: Divided into three sections (front, middle, back) each responsible for different shoulder movements. Essential for shoulder stability and size.

muscles.name: Biceps Brachii
muscles.function: Primary arm flexor; supinates the forearm
muscles.origin: Long head: supraglenoid tubercle; Short head: coracoid process
muscles.details: Most visible arm muscle; consists of two heads that work together for elbow flexion. Critical for arm pulling and flexing movements.

muscles.name: Triceps Brachii
muscles.function: Primary arm extensor; extends the elbow
muscles.origin: Long head: infraglenoid tubercle; Lateral and medial heads: posterior humerus
muscles.details: Three-headed muscle on back of arm; makes up 2/3 of arm mass. Critical for pressing movements and arm extension.

muscles.name: Rectus Femoris
muscles.function: Primary knee extensor; also flexes the hip
muscles.origin: Anterior inferior iliac spine and rim of acetabulum
muscles.insertion: Base of patella and tuberosity of tibia
muscles.details: Central thigh muscle; most visible part of the quadriceps. Works with other quads for powerful leg extension.

muscles.name: Vastus Lateralis
muscles.function: Knee extension; largest and strongest quad
muscles.origin: Greater trochanter, linea aspera, lateral supracondylar line of femur
muscles.insertion: Base of patella and tuberosity of tibia
muscles.details: Largest of the quadriceps; provides most of the leg extension strength. Visible on outer thigh.

muscles.name: Vastus Medialis
muscles.function: Knee extension; stabilizes patella
muscles.origin: Linea aspera, medial supracondylar line, intertrochanteric line of femur
muscles.insertion: Base of patella, medial tibial plateau
muscles.details: Important for knee stability and patellar tracking. The VMO is especially important for knee health.

muscles.name: Biceps Femoris
muscles.function: Primary knee flexor; extends the hip
muscles.origin: Long head: ischial tuberosity; Short head: linea aspera
muscles.details: Outer hamstring; responsible for knee flexion and hip extension. Critical for posterior chain strength.

muscles.name: Semitendinosus
muscles.function: Knee flexor; hip extender; internal rotator of hip
muscles.details: Inner hamstring; works synergistically with other hamstrings for knee flexion and hip extension.

muscles.name: Semimembranosus
muscles.function: Knee flexor; hip extender
muscles.details: Inner hamstring; larger than semitendinosus. Important for knee and hip movements.

muscles.name: Gluteus Maximus
muscles.function: Primary hip extensor; most powerful muscle in body
muscles.origin: Posterior surface of ilium, sacrum, coccyx, sacrotuberous ligament
muscles.insertion: Iliotibial band, gluteal tuberosity of femur
muscles.details: Largest and strongest muscle in the body; responsible for hip extension in running, jumping, and climbing.

muscles.name: Gluteus Medius
muscles.function: Hip abductor; stabilizes pelvis
muscles.details: Important stabilizer for hip and pelvis during single-leg activities. Often weak and needs targeted work.

muscles.name: Rectus Abdominis
muscles.function: Flexes the spine; stabilizes core
muscles.insertion: Xiphoid process and costal cartilages of ribs 5-7
muscles.details: The '6-pack' muscle; creates the aesthetic abdominal appearance. Important for spinal stability and posture.

muscles.name: Transverse Abdominis
muscles.function: Core stabilizer; increases intra-abdominal pressure
muscles.origin: Inguinal ligament, iliac crest, thoracolumbar fascia
muscles.details: Deepest core muscle; acts like a corset around the torso. Essential for spinal stability and proper breathing.
muscles.innervation: Lower intercostal nerves (T7-T12), iliohypogastric, ilioinguinal nerves

muscles.name: External Obliques
muscles.function: Rotates spine; flexes trunk laterally
muscles.details: Visible side abdominal muscle; important for rotational movements and lateral stability.
muscles.innervation: Lower intercostal nerves (T7-T12), iliohypogastric, ilioinguinal nerves

muscles.name: Erector Spinae
muscles.location: Along the spine in the lower back
muscles.function: Extends the spine; maintains posture
muscles.details: Large muscle group on both sides of the spine; essential for maintaining upright posture and spinal extension.

muscles.name: Supraspinatus
muscles.location: Top of scapula, above the spine
muscles.function: Initiates arm abduction; rotator cuff muscle
muscles.insertion: Superior facet of greater tubercle of humerus
muscles.details: Smallest rotator cuff muscle; often irritated in overhead athletes. Critical for shoulder stability.

muscles.name: Infraspinatus
muscles.function: Externally rotates arm; rotator cuff muscle
muscles.insertion: Middle facet of greater tubercle of humerus
muscles.details: Important for preventing shoulder impingement; often underdeveloped in bench-focused lifters.

muscles.name: Subscapularis
muscles.location: Front of scapula (between scapula and ribs)
muscles.function: Internally rotates arm; largest rotator cuff muscle
muscles.details: Largest rotator cuff muscle; works with other rotators to stabilize shoulder joint.

muscles.name: Teres Minor
muscles.function: Externally rotates arm; rotator cuff muscle
muscles.insertion: Inferior facet of greater tubercle of humerus
muscles.details: Works with infraspinatus for external rotation; helps prevent anterior shoulder instability.

muscles.name: Teres Major
muscles.function: Extends, adducts, and internally rotates arm
muscles.details: Often called the 'lat's little helper'; assists latissimus dorsi in pulling movements.

muscles.name: Anterior Deltoid
muscles.function: Flexes and internally rotates arm
muscles.details: Front portion of deltoid; primary mover in pressing movements.

muscles.name: Posterior Deltoid
muscles.function: Extends and externally rotates arm
muscles.details: Back portion of deltoid; often underdeveloped but crucial for shoulder health and balance.

muscles.name: Flexor Carpi Radialis
muscles.function: Flexes wrist and elbow
muscles.details: Primary wrist flexor; important for grip strength and wrist mobility.

muscles.name: Flexor Carpi Ulnaris
muscles.function: Flexes wrist and elbow
muscles.origin: Medial epicondyle of humerus, olecranon process
muscles.details: Assists with wrist flexion; important for grip and wrist stabilization.

muscles.name: Extensor Carpi Radialis
muscles.function: Extends wrist and deviates radially
muscles.details: Primary wrist extensor; helps stabilize wrist during lifting.

muscles.name: Extensor Carpi Ulnaris
muscles.function: Extends wrist and deviates ulnarly
muscles.details: Assists with wrist extension and stabilization.

muscles.name: Brachioradialis
muscles.function: Flexes elbow; helps lift forearm
muscles.insertion: Base of styloid process of radius
muscles.details: Strong forearm flexor; prominent when flexing elbow with neutral grip.

muscles.name: Gastrocnemius
muscles.function: Flexes knee and plantarflexes ankle
muscles.details: Superficial calf muscle; responsible for the visible calf bulge. Works on both ankle and knee.

muscles.name: Soleus
muscles.location: Back of calf (lower portion, under gastrocnemius)
muscles.function: Plantarflexes ankle (primary)
muscles.details: Deep calf muscle; often neglected but important for overall calf development and ankle stability.

muscles.name: Tibialis Anterior
muscles.function: Dorsiflexes ankle; inverts foot
muscles.insertion: Medial cuneiform and base of 1st metatarsal
muscles.details: Lifts the toe during walking; important for gait and ankle health.

muscles.name: Tensor Fasciae Latae (TFL)
muscles.function: Abducts and internally rotates hip; stabilizes knee
muscles.details: Works with IT band to stabilize knee during movement. Often tight and needs mobility work.

muscles.name: Piriformis
muscles.location: Deep in glutes, near sciatic nerve
muscles.function: Externally rotates hip
muscles.details: Deep hip rotator; can compress sciatic nerve if tight, causing pain.

muscles.name: Adductor Longus
muscles.function: Adducts hip; assists in hip flexion
muscles.insertion: Middle third of linea aspera of femur
muscles.details: Part of adductor group; pulls legs together and stabilizes pelvis.

muscles.name: Adductor Magnus
muscles.function: Adducts hip; assists in hip extension and abduction
muscles.insertion: Linea aspera and adductor tubercle of femur
muscles.details: Largest adductor muscle; works with glutes and hamstrings in hip extension.

muscles.name: Gracilis
muscles.function: Adducts hip; assists in knee flexion
muscles.details: Long, thin muscle; the only adductor that crosses the knee joint.

muscles.name: Serratus Anterior
muscles.function: Protracts scapula; stabilizes shoulder blade
muscles.details: Creates the 'wing' look on the side of the torso; important for shoulder stability in pressing movements.

muscles.name: Levator Scapulae
muscles.location: Back of neck, between neck and shoulder
muscles.function: Elevates scapula; extends neck
muscles.details: Small muscle that elevates shoulder blade; often tight from poor posture.

muscles.name: Sternocleidomastoid
muscles.function: Flexes and rotates neck; assists in breathing
muscles.details: Large visible neck muscle; important for neck stability and posture.

muscles.name: Diaphragm
muscles.location: Below the lungs, separating thorax from abdomen
muscles.function: Primary breathing muscle; contracts to inhale
muscles.details: Critical for breathing and core stability during heavy lifts. Proper breathing technique enhances strength.

muscles.name: Palmaris Longus
muscles.function: Flexes wrist; minor player
muscles.details: Weak wrist flexor; absent in ~13% of people without affecting function.

muscles.name: Pronator Teres
muscles.function: Pronates forearm; assists elbow flexion
muscles.origin: Medial epicondyle of humerus, coronoid process
muscles.details: Turns palm downward; assists in grip strength.

muscles.name: Extensor Digitorum
muscles.function: Extends fingers and wrist
muscles.details: Extends all fingers; works with wrist extensors.

muscles.name: Vastus Intermedius
muscles.function: Knee extension
muscles.details: Deep quad muscle beneath rectus femoris; difficult to isolate but important for knee strength.

muscles.name: Iliacus
muscles.function: Flexes hip; primary hip flexor
muscles.details: Often called psoas major when combined; critical for hip flexion in running and jumping.

muscles.name: Psoas Major
muscles.function: Flexes hip; assists in core stability
muscles.origin: Transverse processes of L1-L5 and intervertebral discs
muscles.details: Deep core muscle; when combined with iliacus forms iliopsoas. Important for hip and core.

organs.name: Heart
organs.location: Chest, slightly left of center, between the lungs
organs.size: About the size of a closed fist
organs.details: A muscular four-chambered organ that continuously pumps oxygen-poor blood to the lungs and oxygen-rich blood to the body. Beats approximately 60-100 times per minute at rest.

organs.name: Lungs
organs.location: Chest cavity, on either side of the heart
organs.function: Facilitates gas exchange between air and blood
organs.details: Two spongy organs where oxygen is taken in and carbon dioxide is expelled. The right lung is larger than the left to accommodate the heart.
organs.capacity: Total lung capacity ~6 liters in adults

organs.name: Brain
organs.function: Controls all body functions, processes information, and enables consciousness
organs.details: The command center of the nervous system, containing approximately 86 billion neurons. Divided into two hemispheres connected by the corpus callosum.
organs.bloodSupply: carotid arteries, vertebral arteries, Circle of Willis

organs.name: Liver
organs.location: Upper right abdominal cavity, beneath the right rib cage
organs.function: Filters blood, produces bile, metabolizes nutrients, detoxifies substances
organs.details: The largest internal organ. Performs over 500 vital functions including protein synthesis, glucose metabolism, and blood detoxification.

organs.name: Stomach
organs.location: Upper central abdomen, below the left rib cage
organs.function: Stores and breaks down food using acid and enzymes
organs.details: A muscular J-shaped organ that churns food and mixes it with gastric juices. Secretes gastric acid and pepsin.

organs.name: Small Intestine
organs.location: Lower abdomen, coiled beneath the stomach
organs.details: A long, narrow tube where most digestion and nutrient absorption occurs. Lined with villi and microvilli to increase surface area.

organs.name: Large Intestine (Colon)
organs.location: Lower abdomen, frames the small intestine
organs.function: Absorbs water and electrolytes, forms and stores feces
organs.details: Wider and shorter than the small intestine. Houses beneficial bacteria and completes digestion.
organs.bacteria: Contains trillions of microorganisms aiding digestion and vitamin synthesis

organs.name: Pancreas
organs.location: Behind the stomach, in the upper abdomen
organs.function: Produces digestive enzymes and regulates blood glucose via insulin and glucagon
organs.details: A dual-function organ with exocrine cells producing digestive enzymes and endocrine cells (islets of Langerhans) producing hormones.

organs.name: Kidneys
organs.location: Retroperitoneal space, on either side of the spine at waist level
organs.function: Filters blood to produce urine and regulate electrolytes and fluid balance
organs.filtration: Filters approximately 120-150 liters of blood daily to produce 1-2 liters of urine
organs.details: Bean-shaped organs containing about 1 million nephrons (functional units) each.

organs.name: Urinary Bladder
organs.details: A muscular, hollow organ lined with transitional epithelium that can stretch to accommodate varying volumes of urine.

organs.name: Spleen
organs.location: Upper left abdomen, beneath the left rib cage
organs.function: Filters blood, removes old blood cells, produces white blood cells
organs.details: Largest lymphoid organ. Contains specialized immune cells and stores blood that can be released during emergencies.

organs.name: Thyroid Gland
organs.function: Produces thyroid hormones that regulate metabolism and growth
organs.details: Butterfly-shaped gland that produces T3 and T4 hormones. Contains iodine and regulates metabolic rate.

organs.name: Pituitary Gland
organs.location: Base of brain, in the sella turcica of the sphenoid bone
organs.function: Master endocrine gland regulating hormone production throughout the body
organs.details: Tiny but crucial gland connected to the hypothalamus. Controls growth, reproduction, metabolism, and stress response.

organs.name: Adrenal Glands
organs.function: Produces hormones that regulate stress response, metabolism, and sexual function
organs.details: Small cap-shaped glands with two distinct regions producing different hormones.

organs.name: Esophagus
organs.location: Throat and chest, behind the trachea
organs.function: Transports food from throat to stomach
organs.details: A muscular tube that propels food downward using peristalsis (wave-like contractions).
